text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: CAPACITY ALERT — Dedicated pool `pelion-enterprise-prod` reporting GPU saturation and request queue growth > 95% for 3m. Affected tenant: pelion-enterprise. Autoscale at max (3->3).

sahil: oncall here, looking at graphs now. loading top queues and jobs.

jen: paging in case we need to evict non-critical jobs, I'm near the eviction runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/evict-low-priority).

maria (eng-sre lead): quick ask — do we have burst credit for Pelion? last check they had 0 reserved burst, but we can authorize emergency shared capacity if CS signs off.

elaine: pelion account team — I’m in the loop. Pelion just messaged support: they saw request timeouts at ~11:12 UTC. They asked for immediate mitigation, willing to accept overage billing. I can escalate approval.

kevin: confirming impact — support triage shows 37 user-facing 5xxs in last 10m, most are generation timeouts. No data leak.

sahil: diagnostics: GPU queue length per-shot: gpu-0 42, gpu-1 39, gpu-2 41. Model: redwood/gpt-medium-v2 quantized. KV memory near full -> causes blocks during new sessions. Autoscaler tried to add nodes but pool max_nodes=3.

jen: options: 1) emergency burst to shared-hosted (add 2 gpus) — immediate but billed; 2) evict low-priority tenant jobs (throttles internal tests) — immediate; 3) instruct Pelion to lower concurrency / switch to smaller model variant — needs coordination; 4) degrade Pelion to reduced tokens per request via rate-limiter policy.

maria (eng-sre lead): prefer burst + temporary throttling so customer stays healthy. If CS approves, we'll set burst for 60m and monitor. Need an owner to run the enable command and to post the commit.

incident-bot: runbook suggestion: `runbook:dedicated-pool-burst-approval` — requires a CS sign-off message in thread and ops approval.

elaine: Pelion verbal approval received — they accept emergency burst and overage. I authorise. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Pelion notified: "We are enabling emergency capacity now; ETA ~3m for routing to start. Will follow up with post-incident billing note."

sahil: executing enable-burst now: ```/ops enable-burst --tenant pelion-enterprise --pool pelion-enterprise-prod --gpus 2 --duration 60m --reason "emergency customer burst approved by CS"```

incident-bot: ACTION LOG: sahil ran enable-burst (cmd id: brst-761234). Shared capacity added: +2 gpus. Routing rebalanced.

sahil: traffic shifting — queue lengths dropping. 5xxs returning to baseline. Monitoring for KV cache pressure.

jen: also kicked eviction of internal test jobs (non-prod tag) to free memory. See logs: ```evict_jobs --tag non-prod --pool pelion-enterprise-prod```

maria (eng-sre lead): handoff — I will own the post-mortem and capacity follow-up. Jen, please keep monitoring for 30m and coordinate with infra to raise pool max_nodes if this repeats. Elaine, please document customer approval and billing reconciliation.

elaine: will file the billing note and confirm with Pelion PM. cc @account-bot.

kevin: final customer update sent: "We added temporary capacity and mitigated the spike; investigating root cause and follow-up plan."

incident-bot: SUMMARY: emergency burst authorized and applied (+2 gpus, 60m). Immediate impact mitigated. Owner: maria (eng-sre lead). Next steps: post-incident review, consider raising pool max_nodes or improving autoscale policies for pelion-enterprise.

sahil: marking incident as returning-to-normal. I’ll stay on watch for 30m then handoff to next oncall. :thumbsup:

jen: acknowledged, standing by.

maria (eng-sre lead): thanks team — logging for postmortem.
